text: Analog optical computing has no bit width, only a signal-to-noise ratio. From the shot-noise limit, roughly how many photons per output symbol are required to resolve 2^b distinguishable levels, and what does that imply?
choices: About 2^b photons; precision is essentially free
About b^2 photons; precision scales gently
About 2^(2b) photons — each extra bit costs 4x the light — confining optical computing to about 4-8 bits
A fixed 1,000 photons regardless of b
explanation: The shot-noise limit requires roughly 2^(2b) photons to resolve 2^b levels, so each added bit quadruples the light needed (256 photons at 4 bits, 65,536 at 8 bits), pinning practical optics to 4-8 bits. Choice 0 understates the exponent (it is 2b, not b); choice 1 is the wrong scaling law; choice 3 ignores the exponential dependence entirely.
